approach.method_basis: The Parent learns a recurrent molecular prior and chooses its prepared checkpoint by fixed-noise ancestral valid, connected, distinct molecular yield, with heldout token loss breaking ties. Each objective starts an adaptable copy of that prior and an accepted-only archive; trajectory-balance updates with a learned normalizer and fixed-prior regularization transfer real graph feedback into later neural sampling. One direct neural batch alternates with two graph batches. Accepted neural molecules refresh a score-ranked breeding population and supply a protected descendant at the first graph handoff. Connected-fragment crossover and atom/bond mutations construct temporary novel offspring pools, and accepted-score fingerprint posterior function draws choose the remaining evaluations. The atom-replacement mutation currently changes one element at one site, so moving a ring nitrogen while retaining composition requires multiple separately sampled substitutions.
approach.novelty: Extend the existing atom-replacement menu with a direct positional exchange between a pyridine-like nitrogen and a hydrogen-bearing carbon in the same aromatic six-member ring. The exchange moves the nitrogen while preserving the formula, ring connectivity and substituent attachment positions, making a new local arrangement available in one edit. Earlier Children in this lineage changed prior preparation, replay, flow credit or neural sampling. This Child changes graph generation. A previous graph-walk experiment established that this exchange can yield scored positional isomers but exposed very few of them and missed its score target; the new question is whether the Parent's larger temporary pools and posterior selection turn that same positional channel into useful accepted descendants.

observed_bottleneck: The current Parent n-dd7b8aa31113 completes all supplied replicas with macro mean 0.5501977216134929 and population SD 0.02173839408580094; all 4350 generated submissions are accepted without evaluator invalids or duplicates. Reading its per-seed summary.json, run.log and graph receipts gives 2850 accepted graph descendants, of which 452 strictly beat their best recorded generating parent (157, 145 and 150 across the supplied replicas). Its graph kernel chooses a single atom and replaces its element; it has no coupled composition-preserving ring-nitrogen exchange. The molecular assessment reports rich heteroaromatic families and uneven coverage of useful local functional-group relationships, so adding nitrogen count alone is not the missing capacity. Read-only enumeration on the Parent's 4500 accepted records finds 1559 records with qualifying N/C pairs, 5300 physical pair occurrences and 4039 distinct nonidentity products after deduplication within each record; all enumerated pair constructions preserve formula and sanitize. These products are unscored diagnostics and their counts do not imply useful gains or global novelty. Among 24712 graph attempts without a successful crossover, 9622 have a pair-bearing first-parent source; these are source opportunities, not observed selected atom sites or all post-crossover mutation opportunities. Node n-abcd951ab7cc supplies direct prior evidence: ten accepted exchanges were distinct positional isomers, three beat their source and three became walk states, but the mean paired gain was only 0.0008412882577690054, below its 0.002 target. The limiting behavior tested here is requiring independent element substitutions to explore a conserved-composition ring-nitrogen position, together with the unresolved exposure and selection of that channel.
hypothesis: Extend the existing graph replace_atom option menu with a direct formula-preserving exchange of a neutral aromatic nitrogen and a hydrogen-bearing aromatic carbon in the same six-member ring, retaining the ring connectivity and substituent attachment framework.

finding_summary.headline: Nitrogen exchange yields 20 evaluated positional isomers; endpoint scores rise while direct yield stays weak
finding_summary.insights:
Larger temporary pools successfully expose this conserved-composition channel to real evaluation, but they do not establish that the posterior favors it: 19 of 315 positional alternatives were selected, or 6.03%, compared with the overall pool allocation of 6.25%. Most constructed alternatives therefore remain unscored. The clean cases show that moving a nitrogen can improve a particular accepted molecule, while their negative average and the nearly unchanged total parent-beating count rule out a general improvement in direct offspring yield in this panel. The registered parent-relative yield prediction is contradicted even though physical activation and the endpoint score target are established.

The endpoint gain cannot be assigned to those five local wins. Expanded menus change stochastic search paths and pool competition, and accepted descendants can subsequently breed and train the policy. The evidence does not separate those continuing effects from the immediate nitrogen relocation. The molecular assessment also places a limit on the chemical interpretation: useful ring and functional-group arrangements coexist with reactive peripheral groups, unusual ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry. Preserving formula and attachments can preserve those liabilities as well. The remaining question is which local positional contexts merit evaluation; neither a universally favorable nitrogen position nor improved synthetic plausibility is demonstrated.
finding_summary.results:
The exchange ran 397 times. Every construction preserved molecular formula, bond connectivity and the qualifying aromatic ring; 341 products were different positional isomers and 56 were symmetry-equivalent to their immediate source. Ordinary novelty checks admitted 315 distinct positional alternatives to temporary pools and reserved one for a protected handoff. The posterior selected 19 of those 315 alternatives, and the protected product was also evaluated, establishing 20 accepted positional isomers. One further evaluated molecule contained a symmetry-equivalent exchange after crossover and is excluded from that activation count. All 150 protected handoffs and every announced batch remained valid.

Fourteen evaluated positional isomers came from an accepted parent followed by exactly one exchange. Five beat that parent and nine lost, with a mean score change of -0.030970. All fourteen entered the immediate survivor population, twelve later served as generating parents, and one increased the running best score by 0.000290. The six positional isomers produced after crossover all scored below their best recorded generating parent; their immediate crossed sources were unscored. Across the entire graph channel, strict parent-beating descendants slipped from 452 to 449 of 2,850, and mean child-minus-best-parent score worsened from -0.089170 to -0.103903.

Despite that weak direct yield, the complete three-seed endpoint mean rose from 0.550198 to 0.587094. Paired gains were 0.052557, 0.021169 and 0.036962, giving a mean gain of 0.036896, above the registered 0.002 target. Deco hop, median and sitagliptin means increased; zaleplon and DRD2 means decreased slightly. All 4,350 generated submissions were accepted within the supplied 4,500-evaluation panel.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich medicinal scaffolds coexist with reactive heteroatom bonds, unusual ring geometry and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: All five objectives have complete supplied trajectories, with 900 records and 870 optimizer proposals per objective. The molecules include linked and fused heteroaromatics, saturated cyclic amines, aryl sulfonamides, lactams, ethers, imidates and fluorinated urea/hydrazine chains. This is broad chemical exploration with concentrated upper-score families, rather than a shortage of rings or nitrogen. In the fixed objective order, the digest ring-closure presence rates are 0.9874, 0.9885, 0.992, 0.9943 and 0.9874; aromatic-token presence rates are 0.9782, 0.977, 0.9655, 0.9667 and 0.8437. These are fractions of proposal strings containing the markers, not fractions of their atoms that are aromatic. Read-only RDKit perception of the full optimizer trajectories gives median heavy-atom counts of 25, 31, 30, 33 and 25, and median ring counts of 3, 4, 4, 4 and 2. The corresponding Parent medians are 25, 36, 30, 32 and 24 heavy atoms, and 3, 4, 4, 4 and 3 rings. Nonchiral Murcko scaffold counts in the current proposals are 655, 600, 588, 641 and 532, although many represent local ring edits or enlarged assemblies rather than independent useful core families. Conventional makeable-looking fragments coexist with N-Cl bonds, O-O bonds, imines, hydrazine-derived linkages, strained small rings, conjugated enlarged rings and highly charged oxygen environments. The digest stereocentre-marker rate is 0.0 on every objective; graph perception finds potential tetrahedral centres in 232, 363, 601, 280 and 493 optimizer proposals respectively. Thus unspecified stereochemistry is a real representational gap, rather than evidence that the molecules are all achiral. Synthetic plausibility and drug likeness are mixed. The recorded scores support chemical associations within these samples; they do not establish a synthesis, a binding pose, or a causal contribution from any particular generator edit.

per_task.generated_character: The dominant upper family has a phenyl ring joining a diazine bearing an imidate or imine to a conjugated seven-member oxygen ring. The two highest digest examples each have 24 heavy atoms, two aromatic six-member rings and one nonaromatic seven-member oxepin-like ring. Other high entries replace the imidate with an amidine-containing aryl ether, change diazine nitrogen positions, or use a methoxyindole-carbonyl-imidazole-pyridyl assembly. These are moderately sized, largely unsaturated molecules, with polar groups placed on an extended ring framework. Their functional groups are chemically recognizable, but the imidates, imines and conjugated enol-ether ring make stability and synthetic handling less routine than for ordinary aryl amides. The full proposal median is 25 heavy atoms and three rings; tiny fragments and much larger branched structures also occur. Compared with the Parent, the upper chemistry shifts from fused aza-ring/amide and unusual sulfur-containing families toward linked diazine/oxygen-ring imidates. The median aromatic-ring count falls from three in the Parent to two here, while median total ring count stays at three.
liabilities: The leading imidate/imine and conjugated oxygen-ring combinations warrant scrutiny for hydrolysis, tautomerism and chemical stability; their recorded scores do not measure these properties.

Late examples introduce ring expansion, a small imine-containing ring or thiol substitution without retaining the highest recorded scores. Increased ring or heteroatom complexity is not itself evidence of improved chemistry.
The full proposals include N-Cl and O-O bonds, and the large low-score assemblies can contain multiple unspecified stereocentres.
missing_features: The lowest fragments lack the connected aromatic framework and polar handles shared by the upper families; the largest poor examples lack their moderate size and limited elaboration. Those features are not preserved consistently across the output.

The upper excerpt shows conventional carbonyl chemistry mainly in a separate indole family, while the dominant linked-ring series relies on imidates, imines and amidines. Equally favorable, chemically varied polar-group arrangements within that same linked framework are not established by the shown molecules.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The digest span is 0.0 to 0.49065338146265813, with median 0.163735. The two cited diazine nitrogen positional isomers tie at 0.49065338146265813, so these examples do not show a universal preference for relocating a ring nitrogen. The analogous imine scores 0.4786541264696099, and the alternate diazine imidate scores 0.4789131426105757. Contracting the oxygen ring gives 0.46746448265590934; the cited less-unsaturated seven-member version gives 0.38212123769975087. The separate indole-carbonyl family reaches 0.4586023950591373. Together these observations favor a moderate molecular size and particular ring/polar-group arrangements, with both heteroatom placement and saturation mattering locally. Methane scores 0.0, whereas a 50-heavy-atom multiring amide/ether assembly scores 2.2628488414681176e-49. Neither minimal fragments nor accumulation of rings and polar groups reproduces the upper-score chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The upper excerpt is concentrated on an anilinoquinazoline-like scaffold: a fused aromatic diazine/benzene system linked through NH to a substituted phenyl ring. Methoxy or other alkoxy groups, halogens and a terminal aryl formaldimine recur. The highest example has 28 heavy atoms and three aromatic six-member rings, but also an O-N(Cl)-ethyl substituent containing both N-O and N-Cl bonds. A simpler dimethoxy member has 24 heavy atoms. The fused aza core, arylamine link and ordinary ethers are plausible synthetic building blocks; the N-chlorinated hydroxylamine ether and formaldimine are less conventional final medicinal functionality. Another trajectory ends with nitrogen-dense fused systems, small fused rings and multiple explicitly negative oxygens. The current full median is 31 heavy atoms and four rings, compared with 36 heavy atoms and four rings in the Parent. The Parent upper chemistry included larger linked quinazoline-like systems and carbonyl-bearing piperazine derivatives, so the current prominent family is a smaller connected aza-aromatic arrangement, not newly acquired aromaticity.
liabilities: N-Cl-bearing hydroxylamine ethers and terminal methylene imines introduce reactive functionality into the strongest-scoring family. Even the simpler dimethoxy analogue retains the imine.

Some final structures combine heavily fused small rings with alkoxide-like and N-O anions; the cited multiply negative molecule has no accompanying counterion in its SMILES. Charge and valence validity do not establish a plausible dominant chemical state.
The full optimizer set contains 121 molecules with an O-O bond, and its charged-marker rate is 0.2264. These features are materially present rather than isolated textual curiosities.
missing_features: Many lower-scoring sulfonyl or nitrogen-rich structures lack the specific aryl-NH-diazine connection and alkoxy substitution context shared by the upper molecules. Total aromaticity and nitrogen content do not substitute for this local arrangement.

The highest excerpt does not show broad coverage of different cores retaining an equally favorable attachment pattern; it mostly repeats one aza-aromatic family with peripheral variations. Chemically conservative alternatives to its reactive peripheral groups are only partially represented.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The digest span is 0.2712455185234365 to 0.9410803537101116, with median 0.579468. The N-Cl-containing leader scores 0.9410803537101116 and its cited less-fluorinated analogue scores 0.9369083259163363. The simple dimethoxy scaffold and several chlorinated alkoxy or thioether variants all score exactly 0.9331819976312673 despite differing size and local reactivity. That plateau is consistent with emphasis on the common scaffold and attachment pattern, with limited discrimination among these peripheral groups. A stilbene-sulfone chain terminating in a hydroxamate scores 0.2712455185234365, and a multiaryl sulfone/sulfonamide structure scores 0.29444616217051867. They supply rings and polar atoms without reproducing the upper anilino-aza-ring context. The cited terminal nitrogen-rich fused structures score 0.6068151045584474 and 0.5985804416403786, showing that more ring nitrogens and more fusion alone do not reproduce the leading arrangement.

per_task.generated_character: The upper molecules combine substantial aromatic surfaces with accessible aliphatic amines. The highest example is a 23-heavy-atom dibenzocycloheptane-like tricycle bearing a dimethylaminoethyl chain, phenol and amino substituents. Other high examples use a fused pyrrole/aryl framework with an N-methylpiperidine or dimethylaminoalkyl group. Another seed produces halogenated polycyclic amines carrying an aziridine and an aminoethyl branch. The final excerpt also contains aryl ethers linked to N-methylpyrrolidine or piperazine. These families have recognizable medicinal amine/aromatic organization, although some constrained cores are synthetically demanding and the aziridines deserve separate scrutiny. The full median is 30 heavy atoms, four rings and two aromatic rings, matching the Parent on these descriptors. The Parent leading examples included long-linker arylpiperazines and bridged oxygen-containing aryl amines; the prominent current examples shift toward compact aryl tricycles with shorter aminoalkyl connections. The charged-marker rate of 0.0103 does not imply a shortage of potentially basic centres: ordinary neutral amine SMILES are abundant.
liabilities: The halogenated polycyclic family includes an aziridine, adding a strained nitrogen-containing three-member ring to an already constrained scaffold.

Potential tetrahedral stereocentres occur in 601 of the 870 optimizer proposals, while the digest stereocentre-marker rate is 0.0. The leading amino-substituted tricycle itself has an unspecified tetrahedral centre.

Some high examples combine several amines with phenol, aniline or thiol groups and complicated fused/bridged frameworks. Their ionization, chemical stability and synthetic tractability are not determined by the recorded scalar scores.
missing_features: Several weak chemotypes lack a comparably accessible aliphatic amine in the aromatic framework. Amide, sulfonamide and pyrrole nitrogen do not reproduce the same chemical environment, even when the molecules contain multiple nitrogen atoms.

Stereochemically specified versions of the constrained amine-bearing cores are absent from the proposal strings. Their possible three-dimensional alternatives remain unresolved; the shown scores do not establish which configuration, if any, would be preferable.

The compact dimethylaminoethyl tricycle scores 0.9971131223195837; its extra-phenol analogue scores 0.9918069064419354. The N-methylpiperidine-containing pyrrole/aryl system scores 0.9921820880456957. Thus neither more hydroxylation nor a single required amine ring is supported as a universal rule. At the low end, the aryl amide/sulfonyl structure scores 3.8021829379963674e-05 and the nitroaryl acylhydrazone scores 4.1105044111594925e-05; their nitrogens are not equivalent to the accessible aliphatic amines in the leaders. per_task.generated_character: The leading family joins an alkoxy-substituted phenyl sulfonamide of N-methylpiperazine to a conjugated aza-lactam carrying a methylenedioxy ring. The highest molecule has 37 heavy atoms and four perceived rings: a phenyl, a piperazine, a ten-member conjugated nitrogen-containing ring and a five-member dioxole. Its extended aza ring is marked aromatic by graph perception; it should not be mistaken for an ordinary fused six-member heteroaromatic system. There are two perceived aromatic rings overall. The sulfonamide, piperazine, ethers and carbonyl are familiar groups, but the ten-member conjugated ring creates a substantial geometry and synthetic-plausibility question. A separate high family contains an aminopyridine linked through an alkene to a seven-member diazepinedione and a benzodioxole. Late molecules in another seed join indole-like systems to N-methyl carbonyl rings through oxygen-rich connections, including an O-O-containing cycle. The full median is 33 heavy atoms and four rings, compared with 32 and four for the Parent. The Parent upper family included a more conventional seven-member diazepinone linked to aryl sulfonylpiperazine and methylenedioxy groups; the current leader changes the conjugated ring geometry rather than introducing the familiar functional groups for the first time.
liabilities: The leading ten-member aromatic-coded aza-lactam needs scrutiny of conformation, conjugation and synthetic accessibility. Sanitized aromatic notation alone does not establish a stable, readily makeable geometry.
The late oxygen-rich series contains a cyclic O-O bond and N-O-containing alternatives. The full optimizer trajectories contain 32 O-O-bearing molecules.
Repeated carbonyl, sulfonyl and ether substitution can produce large acceptor-rich structures; the upper score does not imply that further polar-group addition or ring expansion is useful.
missing_features: Low acyclic polyamines and fragments lack the organized ring/carbonyl/aryl relationships present in the upper families; they do not lack nitrogen or, in the polyamine case, molecular size.

The dominant upper series lacks a demonstrated set of conventional ring-geometry alternatives that preserve its useful sulfonylpiperazine, aromatic and carbonyl relationships. The Parent seven-member family and the current separate diazepinedione series show that such chemistry is accessible elsewhere, but the ten-member leading neighborhood remains unusual.

Adding a thiol gives 0.24379205981752294, expanding the dioxole to a six-member oxygen ring gives 0.2426635649223404, and changing the piperazine N-methyl substituent to a sulfonylmethyl group gives 0.24079605482975625. per_task.generated_character: The strongest excerpt is a flexible iodophenoxy ketone linked through a short chain to a hydrazine-derived urea and a fluorinated alkyl group. The leader has 24 heavy atoms, one phenyl ring, an ether, a ketone, a urea carbonyl and an N-N bond; its fluorinated chain contains an unspecified tetrahedral centre. Another high family carries a pyridyl sulfonamide and a small N/O-containing ring attached to a fluorinated seven-member cyclic cumulene. The urea, ketone and aryl ether are recognizable chemistry, but the adjacent N-N bond and the separate cyclic-cumulene family make overall synthetic plausibility uneven. The Parent upper chemistry included fused nitrogen/oxygen heterocycles and fluoroalkenyl ureas, while the current upper excerpt emphasizes a flexible fluorinated hydrazine/urea chain. Thus the changed leading chemistry has fewer rings, despite an overall ring-closure presence rate of 0.9874.

The seven-member cyclic cumulene introduces a strong ring-geometry and strain concern. The digest cumulated-double-bond marker rate is 0.0943, so this type of unsaturation is materially represented in the broader proposal set.

The full proposals contain 91 O-O-bearing molecules and potential tetrahedral stereocentres in 493 of 870 proposals, while the stereocentre-marker rate remains 0.0. Oversized, highly flexible multigroup assemblies also persist at the zero-score end.

The leading fluorinated chain lacks stereochemical specification, and the high excerpt does not establish an equally favorable set of less unusual N-N-free or geometrically restrained alternatives retaining its polar-group spacing. These are coverage gaps, not evidence that a particular extra ring or configuration must improve the objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The digest span is 0.0 to 0.49702898037063575, with median 0.001405. The leader scores 0.49702898037063575, while the version with an additional aryl fluorine scores 0.4779789711749196. Moving one fluorine from the difluoroalkyl terminus to the aryl ring gives a molecule with the same C14H17F3IN3O3 formula as the leader but a score of 0.42289529223448297. Reconnecting the ketone/ether region as an ester-containing analogue gives 0.43350845268587673. Inserting an additional consecutive nitrogen into the aryl-fluorinated urea/hydrazine chain reduces its recorded score to 0.1359300194081745. transferable_gaps.evidence: Upper excerpts include an N-chlorinated hydroxylamine ether, imidates and imines, hydrazine-derived ureas and an S-F substituent; later relatively favorable molecules include a cyclic peroxide. Across the supplied optimizer trajectories, O-O-bearing molecule counts are 14, 121, 6, 32 and 91 in the fixed objective order. A simple dimethoxy aza-aromatic scaffold and several chlorinated alkoxy or thioether variants all receive 0.9331819976312673, illustrating that the observed feedback can leave chemically different peripheral liabilities unresolved.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve conventional local bonding environments while modifying otherwise useful molecular cores.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make candidate construction sensitive to complete local functional-group environments, including the atoms bonded to nitrogen, oxygen, sulfur and halogens. Retain access to conventional stable alternatives when varying an accepted core, so exploration does not depend on adding reactive heteroatom-halogen or heteroatom-heteroatom bonds. Learn any objective-value tradeoff from accepted feedback; these chemical concerns alone do not establish that blanket exclusions would improve scores.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every digest stereocentre-marker rate is 0.0. Direct graph perception finds potential tetrahedral centres in 232, 363, 601, 280 and 493 optimizer proposals in the fixed objective order. The cited compact amino-substituted tricycle, aziridine-containing polycycle and leading fluorinated urea/hydrazine chain all contain unspecified tetrahedral centres.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not express stereochemical alternatives for the many potentially chiral structures it emits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and preserve stereochemical assignments when constructing or changing potentially stereogenic centres, and make chemically feasible configurations available as distinct alternatives where the evaluation interface distinguishes them. Changes in configuration should be separable from changes in connectivity. The supplied observations establish missing specification, not a preferred stereoisomer or a guaranteed score benefit.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The quoted upper molecules include a ten-member conjugated aza-lactam marked aromatic by graph perception, a seven-member cyclic cumulene, aziridine-containing polycycles and several heavily fused small-ring systems. Ring-token presence is already close to universal, and normal phenyl, heteroaryl and cyclic-amine motifs are also present. The missing property is control over ring geometry, not the ability to close rings.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring construction does not consistently constrain conjugation and ring geometry to chemically credible alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Explore ring size, fusion, bond order and saturation with attention to the resulting geometry and functional-group compatibility. Keep conventional ring alternatives available while preserving useful attachment positions, and distinguish changes in ring topology from peripheral decoration. Aromatic notation and valence sanitization should not be treated as proof of a feasible conformation or easy synthesis.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A fluorinated urea/hydrazine pair has the same C14H17F3IN3O3 formula but scores 0.49702898037063575 and 0.42289529223448297 when fluorine is distributed differently between chain and aryl ring. Adding a consecutive nitrogen to a related chain gives 0.1359300194081745 instead of 0.4779789711749196. Elsewhere, two ring-nitrogen positional isomers tie at 0.49065338146265813. The upper amine/aromatic series repeatedly differs from low amide-, sulfonamide- or pyrrole-nitrogen examples in nitrogen accessibility and bonding context. These observations support context-dependent placement, not a universal benefit from another heteroatom or any single relocation.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful functional-group position and electronic context are not reliably retained across molecular edits.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide coordinated alternatives for functional-group orientation, linker position and heteroatom placement while retaining a coherent core and comparable molecular scale. Distinguish accessible amines from amide, sulfonamide, aromatic and hydrazine nitrogen rather than treating element count as the relevant chemical property. Allow current-session observations to determine which local arrangements matter, without encoding a named target or fixed target-specific functional-group recipe.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The zero-score excerpts include methane, acetylene, a 25-heavy-atom acyclic polyamine and 70- or 83-heavy-atom multigroup assemblies. A 50-heavy-atom multiring amide/ether assembly receives 2.2628488414681176e-49. In contrast, quoted upper families include a 23-heavy-atom amine tricycle, a 24-heavy-atom fluorinated polar chain and a 37-heavy-atom sulfonylpiperazine/aza-lactam. These different useful sizes show that neither universal shrinking nor multiplying whole favorable motifs is an adequate chemical rule.
transferable_gaps.gap: Size-changing moves do not consistently preserve a useful connected arrangement of rings, linkers and polar groups.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make growth, contraction and linker changes preserve a recognizable connected core and the relationships among its aromatic, amine and carbonyl groups. Maintain alternatives at multiple chemically coherent scales, with current accepted observations determining the useful size range. Treat fragmentation to tiny pieces and wholesale concatenation as distinct chemistry from controlled local elaboration.

method_name: Genetic GFN: reciprocal learning between a flow policy and graph search
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Genetic GFN: alternately generate molecules with a GFlowNet policy, refine the resulting scored population through graph crossover and mutation, and distill scored descendants back into the policy using rank-weighted off-policy replay. The policy uses trajectory balance with a learned log normalizer and regularization toward a frozen prior. [Kim et al., Section 3](https://arxiv.org/html/2402.05961v4) describe this mechanism. Train the prior only on the permitted unlabeled corpus. Each objective starts with clean policy adaptation, replay and population state initialized from its supplied observations. Use a positive terminal reward increasing with the observed maximization score. Schedule policy and genetic phases around the evaluator's announced feedback; both produce new molecules, and all reward-bearing training records come from accepted observations. Later policy samples must enter genetic populations, and accepted graph descendants must affect subsequent policy updates. Generate further valid, canonical-unique structures to fill announced batches, without corpus ranking or a fixed molecular library. The hypothesis is that learned global proposals propagate local discoveries into new promising regions and then support further graph refinement, raising the mean of five independent final Top-1 scores. Published larger-budget gains do not establish that this reciprocal learning becomes useful quickly enough here.
